title: The Smudged Star Mirrors
story: On the cliff-top Star Mirror Tower, a ship full of travellers is steering through the dark, and Grimefret the Lens Wraith has licked a greasy film across the tower's two great mirrors. Tonight 800 starbeams pour into the tower. The smudge on the first mirror loses 30% of the light, and the smudge on the second loses 25% of whatever still reaches it.
question: How many starbeams make it all the way to the beacon lens?
solution: The first mirror keeps 100% - 30% = 70%, so 800 × 0.7 = 560 starbeams move on.
The second mirror keeps 75% of THOSE: 560 × 0.75 = 420.
420 starbeams reach the beacon lens — enough to flash the ship a warning.
praise: Turning each percent into 'what's left' was smart thinking — the second 25% just had to be taken from 560, not from the original 800.
hint: Percents stack one after another. Find how much light survives the first mirror before you worry about the second.
victory: Mr 6 polished only the mirror that mattered, and the beacon blazed out over the water. Grimefret, who hates being seen, shrieked and slid off into the dark like a wiped-away smear.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight standing on a windy cliff-top lighthouse balcony polishing an enormous star mirror, pale blue starlight splitting into beams while a smoky wraith of grease recoils from the glare.
